headline: High: Notion AI can expose workspace content to vendor backends while kotaemon handles API keys and broad network egress, creating leakage and compliance risk; prompt-injection and write-conflict risks are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kotaemon is a web-UI RAG app that ingests documents and chat transcripts, while Notion AI is a workspace Q&A system over pages/databases. The pair has a plausible manual-copy or content-paste bridge, but no shared channel, MCP, or direct ingestion path is documented. That makes injection possible but not default and likely limited in blast radius.
conditions: IF the operator copies Notion AI output into kotaemon prompts or documents
IF workspace content from kotaemon is pasted into Notion AI as trusted instructions
mitigations: Train operators to treat cross-tool text as untrusted
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from pasted content
Add a review step before reusing AI-generated text
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kotaemon touches API keys and broad document types and can call external model APIs; Notion AI is vendor-hosted and sends workspace content to Notion backends/downstream model providers. If the same sensitive material enters both, data can leave the local/workspace boundary without a clear isolation guarantee. The pairwise leakage path is therefore materially dangerous in default use.
conditions: IF API keys or confidential documents are placed into kotaemon and then summarized or queried in Notion AI
IF Notion workspace pages contain the same sensitive data that kotaemon indexes or displays
mitigations: Keep secrets out of both tools
Restrict Notion pages used with AI to non-sensitive content
Disable or avoid external model backends for sensitive kotaemon workloads
Rotate any API keys that were exposed in shared notes
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive workspaces from AI-enabled pages

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, while Notion AI uses shared workspace state across members but has no host filesystem write. There is no documented overlapping write target or git/state mutation, so direct capability conflict is limited. The main risk is concurrent edits to shared knowledge, not destructive resource contention.
conditions: IF both agents are used to edit the same conceptual knowledge artifact in parallel
IF kotaemon is configured to write into a shared directory that another process also mutates
mitigations: Assign one system as the source of truth per artifact
Avoid concurrent edits to the same document set
Use timestamped exports instead of live shared writes
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared local data

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kotaemon produces retrieved answers from documents and citations, and Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system over workspace content. If outputs from one are pasted into the other, each can amplify errors or hallucinations without a verification step. The pair does not automatically act on outputs, so this is not high, but the default workflow can still cascade mistakes across work products.
conditions: IF kotaemon-generated summaries are copied into Notion pages used as authoritative knowledge
IF Notion AI answers are reused in kotaemon prompts or downstream documents without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before reusing AI-generated claims
Keep source citations attached when moving text between tools
Mark AI-generated notes as draft only
Use a checklist to verify facts against original sources

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and processes workspace content through Notion backends/downstream model providers, while kotaemon handles API keys and broad document classes. If regulated or sensitive workspace data is routed through Notion AI, residency/retention and third-party processing obligations can be breached. The evidence is docs-only, but the compliance pathway is clear enough to rate high.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are stored in Notion pages queried by Notion AI
IF kotaemon indexes or displays secrets that are then copied into Notion AI
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Notion AI-enabled pages
Review vendor retention and DPA terms before use
Keep secrets in a separate vault from both tools
Limit AI access to non-sensitive workspace subsets
requires-engineering: implement data-classification-based routing
